Morphological spectrum of foamy gland carcinoma. (a, b) At low power, a foamy gland carcinoma is characterized by abundant xanthomatous cytoplasm with low N:C ratio, simulating a benign process. Intraluminal, dense, pink, acellular secretions are common. Conventional acinar differentiation (arrow) is also common in foamy carcinoma (a). The nuclei are small and dense; typical malignant nuclear features of prostate cancer are only variably present, making recognition of cancer difficult. Occasional prominent nucleoli and nuclear enlargement are Histologic Variants of Prostate Carcinoma also present (b).

Differentiated adamantinoma. A, at low magnification of this fibro-osseous lesion from the tibia, the stromal element contains numbers foamy histiocytes. It would be easy to overlook the epithelial nest in the top right of the photo. B, a keratin immunostain highlights the epithelial nest together with additional cells that were not visible in the hematoxylin and eosin stained slide.

full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a histological tissue section stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows a fibro-osseous lesion of the bone, characterized by a cellular stroma interspersed with numerous psammomatous or mineralized spherical bodies and trabeculae of woven bone. The stroma contains varied stromal elements and spaces. The histological features are consistent with a diagnosis of desmoid-type fibromatosis or a fibro-osseous lesion such as cementifying fibroma or osteoid osteoma.

blind.description: This is a micrograph of prostate tissue. It shows foamy gland carcinoma, a variant of prostate cancer characterized by abundant xanthomatous cytoplasm and low nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Intraluminal dense pink secretions and small, dense nuclei are also present. The findings are indicative of prostate adenocarcinoma with foamy gland features.

random.description: This is a micrograph showing a bone marrow biopsy specimen stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The tissue demonstrates hypercellularity with prominent bony trabeculae and numerous scattered plump cells embedded in the stroma. The morphological features are characteristic of myelofibrosis, showing replacement of normal hematopoietic elements by fibrous connective tissue and immature cellular elements.
